metric.why: A facility can have enough total cooling and still starve individual racks; airflow and pressure sensors find recirculation, bypass, and leaks that temperature averages hide.
metric.definition: Cubic feet per minute delivered through the room or containment system, and the pressure differential that drives it through equipment rather than around it.

reading.body:
A data center with adequate total cooling capacity can still fail to cool individual racks if airflow recirculates or bypasses equipment, making cubic feet per minute and static pressure the true measure of whether cooling reaches the hardware.

Temperature sensors report the outcome of cooling but not whether air actually flows through the racks that need it. Airflow and pressure readings expose the gaps: warm air recirculating back into intake vents, bypass paths around containment, and leaks that leave some equipment starved while others sit in cold air. This matters for AI because GPU and accelerator density in modern racks generates extreme heat in concentrated spaces. A facility can pass overall temperature checks while individual racks throttle or fail.

Static pressure specifically reveals whether the room's cooling system pushes air through equipment or loses it to uncontended paths. This is an operations problem, not a design one: a well-built data center can degrade over time as door seals wear, cable trays fill, or containment breaches open. Monitoring airflow and pressure catches these failures before hardware begins to fail.
